key_insight: A Distil GPT2 table-to-text framework reported strong disease prediction on small clinical datasets, including thyroid cancer recurrence, rather than addressing drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: The approach may support research into recurrence prediction when labeled clinical data are scarce, but clinical utility remains unestablished.
method: Convert structured clinical records into physician-style text.
Fine-tune Distil GPT2 using original text and GPT4-generated paraphrases to improve minority-class representation.
Use gradient-based explainability to identify influential clinical features.
evidence_signal: Across four public datasets covering heart disease, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, and thyroid cancer recurrence, reported average precision, specificity, sensitivity, and F1-score were 0.96, 0.97, 0.96, and 0.96, respectively.
watch_item: The abstract does not detail external validation or safeguards against leakage from synthetic paraphrases, limiting confidence in real-world generalization.
paper_title: Can GPT Be Used as an Alternative Prediction Model to Traditional Machine Learning and Neural Networks on Low-Volume Clinical Data?
